headline: Approved Rob Kleiner as primary and Sarah Beauregard as backup representatives for city-wide master planning.
summary: Staff presented FY28 capital budget requests, including $450,000 for the Kiwanis Park skate park and $250,000 for cemetery improvements. The committee will vote on these recommendations at its next meeting. Residents also asked that trash cans be returned to Keach Park.

plain_text:
1 | P a g e 
 
 City of Concord, NH   Recreation and Parks Advisory Committee  
Meeting Minutes from October 15, 2026 5:30pm DRAFT 
  
  
Committee Members:), Althea Barton (Ward 1), Robert Kleiner (Ward 2), Sarah Beauregard (Ward 4), Barb Higgins 
(Concord School District), Zoey Murphy (Ward 5), Nick Kotkowski (Ward 6), Mary Miller, Chair (Ward 10), City 
Councilor Michele Horne, Deodonne Bhattarai (Ward 9) and City Councilor Nate Fennessy, Kenny Edwards 
(Merrimack Valley School District), 
 
Absent: Dhan Timsina, (8), Jim Figueira (Ward 3) and Matt Walsh, Deputy City Manager  
 
Staff Members: Laura Bryant Assistant Parks & Recreation Director and David Gill, Director of Parks & Recreation 
 
The meeting was called to order at 5:34 p.m. by Chair Mary Miller.  
 
New Business:  
 
1. Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) for FY28 budget:  David Gill reviewed the CIP process. The process was 
moved up this year due to the retirement of the City Manager. David review staff recommendations as well as 
additional projects that will fall under General Services. 
 
  FY28 Staff Recommendations and will be voted on at the next meeting. 
CIP 60 Kiwanis Park: Shows two phases for new skate park. FY27 Phase 1: Skate Board Park and 
related site improvements. $1 million (donations and grants). In 2025 we were awarded $500,000 
LWCF grant to help with construction. The grant requires a dollar for dollar match. To date we have 
received just over $22,000 in donations from the Skate Park Association. Request City fund $450,000 
to build phase 1 of skate park in FY28. Used to help with 1:1 match requirement plus $50,000 
donations. 
 
CIP 63 (GSD) City Wide Recreation Improvements: Replace two large storage sheds in the Parks. 
Rollins Park and Rolfe Park: $200,000 
CIP 569 Equipment – mowers/other equipment parks and cemeteries. $50,000 - $75,000 (TBA) 
CIP 587 Cemetery Improvements:  Add 2 new columbium and related site improvements: $250,000 
 
In partnership with GSD: CIP 63 GSD City Wide Recreation Improvements:  
o Pool Renovations (Garrison and Rollins remaining in this round of renovations)  
o West Street Ward House and Green Street Community Centers 
o Some items under Memorial Field Complex (buildings, bleachers) 
o GSD handles maintenance of our storage sheds in the parks (Rollins (1), White (1), 
Mem Field (several), Keach (2), Merrill (1) and Rolfe (1)) 
o  
We also work with GSD for our scheduled replacement of our trucks for the Parks and Cemeteries Divisions
2 | P a g e 
 
 
 
2. Donation from Black Ice Pond Hockey Association: David Gill shared with RPAC that the Black Ice Pond 
Hockey Association has made a $4,800.00 donation to cover 20-hours per week for a staff person to open the 
Lodge at White Park for Ice Skating this winter. David will ask Council to accept the donation at the 
November meeting. It will be up to Parks & Recreation to hire a staff person by December 1th or Black Ice 
will ask for the donation back. The committee was very supportive of their donation. 
 
3. Rental Fee Waiver Follow Up: David Gill asked RPAC for clarification on what they are looking for as far 
as the fee waiver policy since he was not at the last meeting. Michele Horne wants it a general idea of what it 
would look like when some one applies. Mary Miller wants it to be a fair process for everyone. David Gill 
asked if all fees should be looked at and RPAC agreed that was not necessary. They would just like a clear 
policy on what steps/ requirements ore necessary to request a fee waiver. David Gill said staff would present 
something for RPAC to review at a future meeting. 
 
4. Review First Year of Keach Park Lights: David Gill reviewed the first year of the field lights at Keach 
Park. He didn’t have the light bill but will bring those to a future meeting once he receives them. The lights 
will be turned off for the season on October 31st. after that staff will begin seasonal maintenance. So far there 
have been no requests for rentals under the lights but there has been a regular adult group on Thursday 
evenings. Michele Horne asked if the wear and tear was more than in past years and David confirmed that it 
was. Nate Fennessy asked if there were still concerns from the neighbors. David confirmed there are still 
concerns such as noise after 9pm, and people driving fast on Newton Ave.  
 
5. Update of City-Wide Master Planning: Those who attended the open house on September 19th said it was 
well attended and a successful kick of to the project. Nick Kotkowski made a motion to nominate Rob Kleiner 
and Sarah Beauregard as the representatives to participate on behalf of RPAC seconded by Nate Fennessy, 
approved. Rob Kleiner will be primary and Sarah Beauregard as back up. 
 
Old Business: David Gill gave quick update on the following:  
 
 Memorial Field Master plan – City Council at their Oct 2026 meeting approved $600,000 of city funds and 
accepted a $600,000 donation from Concord School District to allow the final design and permitting for new 
Master Plan to be completed. Moving forward it will be a 12-month process for design, there are several 
grants to apply for. 
 
 Bike Park Planning – The city will handle the environmental review, if the review comes back and shows the 
site as appropriate the project will move forward to next steps. 
 
 Skate Park at Kiwanis Park – still working toward the fundraising goals of 500K to match LWCF grant
3 | P a g e 
 
 Snowmaking Operations at Beaver Meadow Golf Course in partnership with SkitheBeav – The SkitheBeav 
group will be coming to Council by their December meeting with the final 15K in December to complete their 
100K donation. They have committed to paying for the installation of under water pipes and new transformer 
and underground power lines needed for the snowmaking operation. In addition, they have agreed to pay for 
all utility expenses related to snow making (power and water). 
 
 David Gill shared on final piece of very positive news. Miracle Recreation will feature the new playground at 
White Park in their campaign for inclusive playgrounds for this upcoming year. They were in town last week 
recording a commercial with local kids. 
 
5 minutes public input: 
Christine Rioux came with a letter she had sent to the City Clerk regarding trash cans at Keach Park. She gave 
a copy of her letter to all RPAC members and said she would return in November when that item was on the 
agenda. 
 
Charm Camacho also came to ask that the trash cans be put back in Keach Park. David Gill indicated the City 
Council Referral will be discussed at the next meeting She indicated she will also return for the November 
meeting. Deodonne Bhattarai asked if David could also have the trash collection cost analysis available at that 
meeting. 
 
 
 
Motion was made by Mary Miller to end the meeting at 6:32pm, seconded by Sarah Beauregard and approved.  
 
Next RPAC meeting scheduled for Thursday November 19, 2026 at 5:30pm.  
 
Submitted by Laura S. Bryant, Assistant Parks & Recreation Director
